title: Lexicon entry (open-greek-lexica 0.3.0)
description: One entry of a lexicon, one JSON object per line in entries/NNNN.jsonl. The entry text is plain text; senses, citations, cross-references and typographic marks point into it with character spans (standoff markup), so the text needs no escaping or sanitizing.

id.description: Stable id: lexicon id, a colon and a local id that is never reused for another entry.

headword.description: The headword as printed, without the flag symbols and homograph number, which have their own fields. Several printed forms are joined with ', '.

key.description: Normalized lookup key of the first printed form (see key_normalization in the manifest). It starts with a Greek letter (a capital or small letter of the Greek blocks: not a sign, numeral sign, ypogegrammeni or prosgegrammeni, nor a Coptic letter), or with a hyphen for a suffix; pattern is key_pattern() in lexica_format.py.

alt_keys.description: Further lookup keys: other printed forms and, where the source gives one, a standard lemma spelling. Each starts with a Greek letter or a hyphen.

fold.description: The letters of key (fold version 1 in the manifest's key_normalization): no breathings, accents, diaeresis, iota subscript, hyphens or spaces, σ for ς. For forgiving search.

homograph.description: The printed homograph number, or null.

flags.description: Signs printed before the headword, in printed order. What each means is stated in the lexicon's README.

quality.description: How far the entry can be trusted: transcribed-checked (a transcription checked against the print), ocr-headword-checked (OCR text whose headword and start passed the build's checks, which catch misreadings but do not prove a headword right), ocr (OCR text with a doubtful headword or start; see source.review).

text.description: The whole entry as plain text in printed order, starting with the flags and headword. No inline markup.

page_breaks.description: Page or column breaks inside the entry: the new page starts at this text offset.

source.description: Identifiers in the source encoding, for tracing; free-form per lexicon. LSJ8 entries record perseus_id, the id of the matching LSJ9 entry in the Perseus encoding, where one matches.

corrections.description: Ids of the records in corrections.json that changed this entry.

span.description: [start, end) character offsets into the entry text (Python string indices, Unicode code points).

loc.description: Printed volume, page and column. Null when the lexicon has no volumes or columns or the value is unknown.

label.description: The printed label, without brackets: 1, a, β, II.

path.description: Labels from the top level down, joined with dots: 7.a. Unique within the entry.

label_printed.description: False when the label was added by the encoder and is not in the print.

printed.description: The reference as the lexicon prints it (Cunliffe: Ξ 113, or 143 for a further line of the same book).

encoded.description: The reference as the source encoding writes it, when it differs from the print.

urn.description: CTS URN of the cited passage.

address.description: Corpus address work:locus in the corpus release named in the manifest, or null when the passage is not in it.

sense.description: Path of the innermost sense containing the citation.

quote.description: The quoted words the reference supports, as printed.

problem.description: Why the reference could not be read normally (no-target, not-homer, text-differs-from-link, unparsed-text, no-such-book, continuation-changes-book, continuation-without-book).

target.description: Entry id, or null when the target is not in the lexicon.

encoded.description: The reference as the source encoding writes it, when the text gives it in the printed form.

mark.description: A typographic or editorial span. A correction mark covers the corrected text and also has correction, original, error_in and reason.

correction.description: correction mark: id of the record in corrections.json.

original.description: correction mark: the reading before the correction: the printed form for a reference, the source text for other elements, null when the correction moved text into the entry.

error_in.description: correction mark: whether the printed book or the source encoding was wrong.

reason.description: correction mark: the record's one-line summary.

print_reading.description: correction mark: the print's own reading, when it differs from both original and corrected text.
